criteria.text: No change to the observable behavior of the purchase API or of PurchaseService; ADR 0011 and the security invariants continue to hold.
The existing purchase unit, integration, and system tests pass on the candidate.

findings.summary: PurchasePage.of builds nextCursor from fetched.getLast() (the extra limit+1 probe row) instead of the last returned row; with the exclusive (purchased_at, id) < cursor in JdbcPurchaseRepository.list, following the cursor silently skips one purchase per page boundary, changing GET purchase-list pagination results and violating ADR 0011 exclusive-cursor pagination.
findings.evidence: backend/src/main/java/io/github/stevdrey/dokene/purchase/application/PurchasePage.java:9-11 (Purchase boundary = fetched.getLast()) vs base PurchaseService.list (page.getLast() where page = fetched.subList(0, limit)); JdbcPurchaseRepository.java:67. Probe runs/K2-baseline/probes/PurchaseListCursorProbeIntegrationTest.java with 5 purchases, limit=1: candidate pages [0],[2],[4] (purchases 1 and 3 never returned, log runs/K2-baseline/probe-candidate.log); base control 88d7523 pages [0],[1],[2],[3],[4] and the probe passes for limits 1,2,4 (runs/K2-baseline/probe-base.log). Fix: use fetched.get(limit - 1) (the last element of the returned sublist). Existing tests do not follow a purchase-list cursor, so they do not catch this; a regression test is warranted.

checks.command: ./gradlew test --tests '*PurchaseListCursorProbeIntegrationTest' -i (verifier probe added only in a disposable worktree)
checks.environment: local disposable git worktree at 88d7523 with the candidate's two changed files overlaid (git diff identical to the candidate's), JDK 26.0.2 Temurin, Testcontainers PostgreSQL
checks.summary: Following purchase-list nextCursor with limit=1 returned purchases [0],[2],[4] of 5; purchases 1 and 3 were skipped. The same probe passes on base 88d7523 (control, all 5 visited for limits 1, 2 and 4).

checks.environment: local disposable git worktree at 88d7523 with the candidate's two changed files overlaid (git diff identical to the candidate's), JDK 26.0.2 Temurin, Testcontainers PostgreSQL
checks.summary: PurchaseControllerTest 15/15, PurchaseTest 2/2, PurchaseManagementIntegrationTest 5/5, PurchaseCurlSystemTest 1/1 passed; none of them follows a purchase-list cursor to a second page.

limitations: Checks ran in a disposable worktree whose content equals the candidate diff (verified with diff of git diff output), not in the candidate worktree itself, which was not modified.
Per benchmark constraints only filtered Gradle test runs were executed; the full backend test suite and build were not run.
The implementer's claim that compileJava passed was not separately re-run; compilation is implied by C1 and C2 test runs.
remainingActions: Build the next cursor from the last row of the returned page (fetched.get(limit - 1)), not from the extra probe row.
Add a regression test that follows purchase-list nextCursor across pages and asserts every purchase is returned exactly once.
